subject: Proposal: 16→32 GPU upgrade — tiered reserved-hour pricing and throughput SLAs
messages:
From: Alex Mercer <alex@cumuluslabs.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal coming up — interested in moving to 32 GPUs during renewal

Hi Sofia,

Our renewal with Redwood is up next quarter. We’re running heavier LLM workloads and the ops team asked whether we can move from our current 16-GPU reserved pool to 32 during the renewal window. The big asks from our side are: a revised per-hour reserved rate, a short-term burst/balancing option while we redistribute load, and a committed throughput SLA for peak business hours.

Can we get a proposal that lays out the pricing for 32 reserved GPUs (per-hour), a staged transition plan (so we don’t double-bill during migration), and what throughput guarantees you can commit to?

We’d like to share the plan with finance and legal by the 23rd.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Mercer
Head of Platform, Cumulus Labs
alex@cumuluslabs.com

--
Attachment: Cumulus-current-usage-summary.csv (attachment referenced)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@cumuluslabs.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-16T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — interested in moving to 32 GPUs during renewal

Alex — thanks for the clear ask. We can definitely put together a formal amendment that upgrades you 16→32 reserved GPUs at renewal and outlines a staged migration with blended billing during the handover.

High-level approach (we’ll send a formal packet by 3/18):
- Two pricing options: 1) Front-loaded reserved rate (single blended per-hour for full 32) and 2) Tiered reserved-hours (base 16 at core rate, incremental 16 at stepped rate).
- Short-term burst pool (30 days) to absorb traffic while you move model replicas — billed at a reduced ‘burst’ rate, not full reserved hours.
- Throughput SLO: target token throughput per GPU for business-critical window (we need to align on your peak hours and baseline).
- Mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones, testing window, and rollback criteria.

I’ll loop Aditya to surface the concrete numbers and Marissa for the rollout ops checklist. Can you share your current peak-hours (local time) and target 95th-percentile tokens/sec requirement? That will let us size the throughput guarantee.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Principal Account Manager, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

--
Attachments: none

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@cumuluslabs.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-17T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Renewal coming up — interested in moving to 32 GPUs during renewal

Alex — sharing two practical pricing constructs for the 16→32 upgrade; picking one will let us draft the amendment and updated invoice. Numbers are illustrative and negotiable — happy to refine once we confirm peak throughput and contract term length.

Option A — Blended 32 Reserved (simple)
- Per-hour reserved rate: $6.50 / reserved GPU-hour (applies to all 32 GPUs)
- Minimum commit: 12 months
- Includes 5% dedicated burst credits for 30 days during migration

Option B — Tiered Reserved Hours (gradual, lower incremental cost)
- Base 16 GPUs: $6.95 / reserved GPU-hour (current core rate)
- Additional 16 GPUs (incremental): $5.10 / reserved GPU-hour (stepped discount for expansion)
- Billing during migration: blended billing for migration week only (we prorate hours by hourly usage to avoid double-charging)
- Minimum commit: 12 months; incremental pool can be flexible after 90 days with 30-day notice

Throughput guarantee proposal (draft):
- Committed 95th-percentile token throughput of X tokens/sec per GPU during Peak Window (09:00–17:00 PT) — final number pending your telemetry.
- Deduction credits: if we miss the 95th-percentile SLA for more than 2 days in a month, Cumulus receives a credit equal to 3% of that month’s reserved spend per missed day.

Next steps: if you prefer Option A we’ll issue an amendment with a single rate. Option B keeps your effective marginal rate lower on extra GPUs. I’ve attached a spreadsheet with cost scenarios.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.com

--
Attachments: tiered-reserved-hour-pricing.xlsx

From: Alex Mercer <alex@cumuluslabs.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya.s@cumuluslabs.com>
Date: 2027-03-18T10:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal coming up — interested in moving to 32 GPUs during renewal

Thanks Aditya — useful framing. A few clarifications from our side:
1) We’re leaning toward the Tiered Reserved Hours (Option B) because keeping the base rate steady helps our forecasting. The incremental $5.10/hour looks appealing.
2) Token throughput: for peak window (09:00–17:00 PT) we need a committed 95th-percentile aggregate throughput of 1.8M tokens/sec across the fleet (this is what our SREs quantified).
3) Burst pool: please clarify how burst credits are redeemed and whether they can be consumed across multiple days in the 30-day migration period.

A couple of asks from finance/legal: can you provide a one-line SLA credit structure and a one-page summary of billing during migration? We’ll need those for procurement to approve the change before the 23rd.

If you can get a redlineable amendment + cost table by EOD 3/18, I’ll run to procurement and loop legal.

Best,
Alex

--
Quoted: "Aditya Rao"

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Alex Mercer <alex@cumuluslabs.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-03-20T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Draft amendment and contract notes for Cumulus Labs 16→32 upgrade

Alex / Priya — attaching the draft amendment and a short summary of proposed contract language to streamline procurement review. Key legal points called out:
- Term: 12 months from effective date (option to renew with 30 days’ notice).
- Pricing: reflect Option B (tiered) in Schedule A with the exact per-hour values and an example monthly invoice.
- Migration billing: explicit clause that during the defined migration window (up to 14 days) the customer will be billed based on actual GPU-hours consumed; any overlapping hours (e.g., both old and new pool active) will be prorated so customer is not double-billed.
- SLA credits: capped at 15% of monthly reserved spend; process for claiming credits includes automated telemetry report and a 10-business-day cure period for Redwood to remediate before credits are applied.
- Data & security: reaffirm existing SOC2 terms and no model/data retention beyond contract scope.

If those points look good I’ll upload the amendment to DocuSign and share the link. Also noted the throughput requirement — Aditya, can you confirm whether 1.8M tokens/sec 95th aggregate is feasible with the proposed pool and whether any further tuning (quantization / batching) would be needed to avoid chronic SLA misses?

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com
